summary.text: Sarah McBride is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Delaware's at-large U.S. House seat, which she won in 2024. A Wilmington native, she worked in Democratic politics and LGBTQ advocacy, wrote a 2018 memoir and served in the Delaware State Senate from 2020 until joining Congress. In the House she serves on the Foreign Affairs and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Wilmington, Delaware, in 1990; her official biography says she grew up in Wilmington and graduated from the Cab Calloway School of the Arts.
Earned a bachelor's degree from American University in 2013.

Worked for former Gov. Jack Markell and the late Attorney General Beau Biden, and served as national spokesperson for the Human Rights Campaign; Ballotpedia also lists her as a national press secretary there and as having worked at the Center for American Progress and the White House during the Obama administration.
Led the effort to pass a non-discrimination law in Delaware before entering the legislature; former Gov. Markell awarded her the Order of the First State.
Published a 2018 memoir, "Tomorrow Will Be Different," with a foreword by President Joe Biden, and has taught public policy at the University of Delaware.

Served as state senator for Delaware's First Senate District from 2020 to 2025, succeeding Harris McDowell. Her office highlights the Healthy Delaware Families Act (paid family and medical leave) and the Protect Medicaid Act of 2024.
Elected to the U.S. House in November 2024, defeating Republican John Whalen III; CNN reported she became the first openly transgender person elected to Congress.

Committee assignments in the 119th Congress are the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the Committee on Foreign Affairs. She has served on the boards of the Delaware Art Museum, Delaware Colleges of Art and Design and Equality Delaware.
